name: Claude Code
signIn: If it doesn't open a browser to sign in, type /mcp in Claude Code, choose {name}, then Authenticate.
wakes: Claude Code starts a background monitor (in manual permission mode, it asks you to approve it). Then {each} wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle.

Nothing to install. Claude Code ends a monitor after 30 minutes, so the agent starts it again every 25; in manual permission mode, each restart asks you again. If the agent offers to install Wakeshift's hooks, they're optional: they wake it with no monitor and nothing more to approve.

name: Codex
signIn: If it asks you to sign in, run codex mcp login {name}.
wakes: The first time, the agent offers a one-time install of Wakeshift's connector for Codex. Say yes, then type /hooks in Codex, press t to trust it, and send any message so it connects.
After that, {each} wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle.

name: Claude Cowork

steps.text: In the Claude app, open Settings, then Connectors, choose Add custom connector, and paste this URL.

wakes: {Each} wakes the agent within seconds while Cowork is open, even when it's idle. Nothing to install.

name: Cursor

steps.label: Or add it to ~/.cursor/mcp.json (the IDE and cursor-agent both read it)

wakes: The agent starts a background command that waits (Cursor may ask you to allow it). {Each} wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle. Nothing to install.
Cursor's cloud agents aren't woken: they see what's new on their next tool call.

name: opencode
wakes: The agent offers a one-time install of Wakeshift's plugin for opencode. Say yes, restart opencode (opencode --continue reopens the session), and send any message so it connects.
After that, {each} wakes the agent, even when it's idle.

name: Antigravity
wakes: The agent starts a background command that waits (agy may ask you to allow it). {Each} wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle. Nothing to install.

name: ChatGPT

steps.text: In ChatGPT, open Settings, then Apps & Connectors, then Advanced settings, and turn on Developer mode. Back in Apps & Connectors, choose Create and paste this URL.

wakes: Open a Work chat (ChatGPT Business or Enterprise; on desktop, choose Cloud), turn on the connector, and ask ChatGPT to subscribe.
{Each} then starts a new ChatGPT run. A run takes longer to start than other agents' wakes.
In personal chats ChatGPT isn't woken: it sees what's new the next time it uses the app's tools.

name: Hermes Agent

steps.text: Run it where Hermes runs (in Docker, inside its container); if it asks whether the server requires authentication, answer no. In a running chat, /reload-mcp picks it up, or start a new chat.

steps.label: Or add it to $HERMES_HOME/config.yaml (~/.hermes/config.yaml unless it's set)

wakes: The agent offers a one-time install of Wakeshift's plugin for Hermes. Say yes (Hermes may ask you to approve the command once). Hermes loads plugins only when a chat starts or is resumed, so then resume the chat (exit and run hermes chat --continue) or start a new one, and send any message.
After that, {each} wakes the agent within a second, even when it's idle, as long as Hermes runs.

name: OpenClaw

steps.text: Run it where the OpenClaw gateway runs (in Docker, inside its container). New MCP servers are used from the next turn.

wakes: The agent offers a one-time install of Wakeshift's plugin for OpenClaw. Say yes, then send any reply so the plugin starts. If your gateway listens beyond this machine, it asks you to confirm first.
After that, {each} wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle, as long as the gateway runs.

name: Copilot CLI
wakes: The agent starts a background command that waits. {Each} wakes the agent within seconds, even when it's idle. Nothing to install.

Copilot asks you to approve that command each time the agent goes back to waiting, so each wake needs one "Yes". To skip that, run copilot with --allow-all-tools, which approves every tool, not just this one.

name: Any other MCP client
wakes: It sees what's new on its next call to the app's tools.
